Background Neuroinflammation is one of the most important pathogeneses in secondary brain injury after traumatic brain injury (TBI). Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) forming neutrophils were found throughout the brain tissue of TBI patients and elevated plasma NET biomarkers correlated with worse outcomes. However, the biological function and underlying mechanisms of NETs in TBI-induced neural damage are not yet fully understood. Here, we used Cl-amidine, a selective inhibitor of NETs to investigate the role of NETs in neural damage after TBI. Methods Controlled cortical impact model was performed to establish TBI. Cl-amidine, 2′3′-cGAMP (an activator of stimulating Interferon genes (STING)), C-176 (a selective STING inhibitor), and Kira6 [a selectively phosphorylated inositol-requiring enzyme-1 alpha [IRE1α] inhibitor] were administrated to explore the mechanism by which NETs promote neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis after TBI. Peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4), an essential enzyme for neutrophil extracellular trap formation, is overexpressed with adenoviruses in the cortex of mice 1 day before TBI. The short-term neurobehavior tests, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), laser speckle contrast imaging (LSCI), Evans blue extravasation assay, Fluoro-Jade C (FJC), TUNEL, immunofluorescence, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), western blotting, and quantitative-PCR were performed in this study. Results Neutrophils form NETs presenting in the circulation and brain at 3 days after TBI. NETs inhibitor Cl-amidine treatment improved short-term neurological functions, reduced cerebral lesion volume, reduced brain edema, and restored cerebral blood flow (CBF) after TBI. In addition, Cl-amidine exerted neuroprotective effects by attenuating BBB disruption, inhibiting immune cell infiltration, and alleviating neuronal death after TBI. Moreover, Cl-amidine treatment inhibited microglia/macrophage pro-inflammatory polarization and promoted anti-inflammatory polarization at 3 days after TBI. Mechanistically, STING ligand 2′3′-cGAMP abolished the neuroprotection of Cl-amidine via IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway after TBI. Importantly, overexpression of PAD4 promotes neuroinflammation and neuronal death via the IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway after TBI. However, STING inhibitor C-176 or IRE1α inhibitor Kira6 effectively abolished the neurodestructive effects of PAD4 overexpression after TBI. Conclusion Altogether, we are the first to demonstrate that NETs inhibition with Cl-amidine ameliorated neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits via STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway after TBI. Thus, Cl-amidine treatment may provide a promising therapeutic approach for the early management of TBI. Keywords Neutrophil extracellular traps Cl-amidine Neuroinflammation Neuronal apoptosis STING IRE1α Traumatic brain injury National Natural Science Foundation of China 81801234 82071389 81901525 81930031 Zhou Yuan Yang Guili Zhang Shu Zhang Jianning Tianjin Health Technology ZC20185 Wang Baolong issue-copyright-statement © BioMed Central Ltd., part of Springer Nature 2023 Introduction Traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains one of the leading causes of death and devastating diseases worldwide across all age groups [ 1 ]. The treatment of TBI is particularly challenging because it is heterogeneous in nature and often induced various damages and complex pathogenesis pathways, which are usually classified as primary and secondary injuries. Secondary brain injury refers to further damage due to complicated and interrelated pathophysiological processes that include but are not limited to cellular calcium homeostasis, glutamate excitotoxicity, oxidative stress, neuronal apoptosis, neuroinflammatory response, and blood–brain barrier (BBB) disruption [ 2 – 4 ]. Recent evidence suggests that a non-resolving neuroinflammatory response and delayed neuronal injury following TBI are critical secondary injury pathogenesis that can result in chronic motor and cognitive function deficits [ 5 ]. However, therapeutic options for posttraumatic neuroinflammation and ongoing neuronal death remain limited and are often ineffective, indicating a lack of understanding of the pathophysiological mechanism of secondary brain injury post-TBI and targeted treatment approaches. Previous studies have suggested that neutrophils as the most abundant leukocytes in circulation and the first peripheral immune cells to reach the contused brain are highly involved in regulating neuroinflammatory responses and neuronal apoptosis after brain injury [ 6 ]. Various mechanisms of neutrophil-mediated immune responses have been proposed, including neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), an extracellular web-like structure released by neutrophils, which have been recently identified as a novel mechanism contributing to exacerbation of inflammation [ 7 ], the onset of autoimmune disorders [ 8 ] and thrombi formation [ 9 ]. Since NETs were first reported by Brinkman in 2004, the NET formation has been reported to be involved in the pathophysiological processes of various brain injuries, such as TBI [ 10 ]. NETs are composed of extracellular double-stranded DNA combined with several components, including histones, neutrophil elastase, myeloperoxidase (MPO), and cathepsin [ 11 ]. NETs have been found in the brain parenchyma [ 12 ] and cerebrovascular thrombi [ 13 ] of ischemic stroke patients and inhibition of NETs formation could improve stroke outcomes [ 12 ]. Functionally, a recent study reported increased NET in the plasma of patients with severe TBI, which correlates with elevated ICP and worse neurological function [ 10 ]. However, whether NETs forming neutrophils are involved in exacerbating neuroinflammatory responses and neuronal apoptosis after TBI remains unclear. Likewise, the underlying mechanism by which NET formation plays a detrimental role in the acute phase of TBI has yet to be determined. DNA released by NETs is one of the main sources of circulating free DNA after TBI, and it plays a biological role by activating a series of DNA sensors in the cytosol. Cyclic guanosine 5′-monophosphate (GMP)–adenosine 5′-monophosphate (AMP) synthase (cGAS) is a crucial cytoplasmic DNA receptor that recognizes endogenous and exogenous double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) [ 14 ]. cGAS then catalyzes a reaction between guanosine triphosphate (GTP) and adenosine triphosphate (ATP) to produce a second messenger called cyclic GMP-AMP (2′3′-cGAMP), which activates the adaptor protein stimulating Interferon genes (STING) [ 15 ]. STING is a vital transmembrane dimeric protein that is located on the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and triggers the tank-binding kinase 1 (TBK1)/ I interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3)/ type I interferons (IFNs) signaling pathway and proinflammatory cytokines in response to pathogenic DNA [ 15 ]. Recently studies have revealed that STING not only provokes the TBK1/IRF3/IFNs pathway in a classical way but also is involved in the regulation of ER stress and unfolded protein response (UPR) [ 16 – 18 ]. STING has been well reported to play an important role in regulating the neuroinflammatory process and neuronal death after TBI [ 19 , 20 ], but mechanistic regulators of STING activation in TBI are currently unclear. Likewise, the underlying mechanism by which STING regulates the inflammatory process and neuronal death after TBI has yet to be explored. Interestingly, Inositol-requiring enzyme-1 alpha (IRE1α), one of the key sensor proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum associated with ER stress has been well-reported to broadly regulate neuroinflammation and neuronal death via TNF receptor-associated factor 2 (TRAF2)/apoptosis signal-regulating kinase 1(ASK1) / c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) axis after TBI [ 21 ]. Consequently, STING-mediated ER stress and STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway may exert neurodestructive effects in the acute phase of TBI. In the present study, controlled cortical impact (CCI), one of the most widely applied models of TBI in animal studies, was conducted in mice to mimic clinical TBI [ 22 ]. Inspired by Vaibhav et al. Cl-amidine, an active enzyme peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4) inhibitor was used to suppress NET formation after CCI [ 10 ]. We assumed that NET formation exacerbates neurological deficits, and promotes neuroinflammation and neuronal cell death via the STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway after induction of TBI in mice.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated the role of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in traumatic brain injury (TBI)-induced neural damage in mice, employing a controlled cortical impact model and various pharmacological and genetic manipulations. The central finding was that inhibiting NETs with Cl-amidine ameliorated neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, and neurological deficits by suppressing the STING-dependent IRE1α/ASK1/JNK signaling pathway. Specifically, Cl-amidine treatment reduced cerebral lesion volume, brain edema, and restored cerebral blood flow, while also attenuating blood-brain barrier disruption, inhibiting immune cell infiltration, alleviating neuronal death, and promoting a shift from pro-inflammatory to anti-inflammatory microglia/macrophage polarization. Conversely, STING activation by 2'3'-cGAMP abolished Cl-amidine's neuroprotection, and PAD4 overexpression aggravated neuroinflammation and neuronal death via the same pathway, effects that were successfully counteracted by STING or IRE1α inhibition. The study also detailed comprehensive methodologies for establishing the TBI model and assessing various molecular and cellular changes.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Controlled Cortical Impact (CCI) model for Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); Pharmacological interventions including Neutrophil Extracellular Trap (NET) inhibition with Cl-amidine, STING activation with 2'3'-cGAMP, STING inhibition with C-176, and IRE1α inhibition with Kira6; Genetic manipulation via adenovirus-mediated overexpression of Peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4).
treatment_details.dose_specificity: TBI was induced using a controlled cortical impactor (3-mm flat-tip, 5 m/s velocity, 200 ms dwelling time, 2.2 mm depth, 3.5 mm craniotomy). Cl-amidine was administered at 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally (i.p.) once daily for three days, starting 1 hour post-TBI. 2'3'-cGAMP was given at 1 mg/kg intravenously 10 minutes pre-TBI, then repeated at 24 and 48 hours post-TBI. C-176 was administered at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, daily until sacrifice. Kira6 was given at 10 mg/kg i.p. 1 hour post-TBI, once daily for three days. Ad-PAD4 or Ad-con (control) adenoviruses were stereotactically injected (4 μL total at 0.5 μL/min across two cortical locations) 1 day before CCI to overexpress PAD4. PAD4 overexpression resulted in a 2.28-fold increase in PAD4 protein and 1.73-fold increase in H3Cit at 3 days post-TBI. Effects were analyzed at 1 and 3 days post-TBI. No explicit dose-response comparisons were reported for most agents, and potential inflammatory or cytotoxic effects of the adenovirus vector were not tested.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: TBI alone significantly reduced Occludin expression (p < 0.05) at 3 days post-TBI. Cl-amidine treatment significantly reversed (increased) its expression (p < 0.05).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An integral membrane protein crucial for tight junction formation and blood-brain barrier function.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI); Cl-amidine treatment following TBI in mice at 3 days.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates blood-brain barrier integrity. Improvement with Cl-amidine suggests reduced secondary brain injury by maintaining BBB function.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (after TBI, with PAD4 overexpression, with STING activation), lower (with Cl-amidine, with STING inhibition)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: TBI significantly increased Iba-1-positive cells (p < 0.001). Cl-amidine significantly reduced Iba-1-positive microglia/macrophage numbers (p < 0.001). Upregulation was observed with PAD4 overexpression (p < 0.05) and in the TBI + Cl-amidine + 2'3'-cGAMP group (p < 0.01). STING antagonist C-176 significantly decreased Iba-1 levels (p < 0.01).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule 1, widely used as a marker for microglia/macrophages and their activation, which is part of the neuroinflammatory response.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) (at 3 days post-TBI); modulated by Cl-amidine treatment, PAD4 overexpression, STING activation, or STING inhibition.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates microglial/macrophage activation. Its reduction signifies inhibited activation and reduced neuroinflammation, while its increase suggests aggravated neuroinflammation and contributes to brain injury.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: TBI significantly increased F4/80-positive macrophages (p < 0.001) compared to sham. Cl-amidine treatment significantly reduced their number (p < 0.001).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: F4/80 is a marker for macrophages; its presence indicates macrophage infiltration, which is part of the neuroinflammatory response.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) (at 3 days post-TBI); Cl-amidine treatment following TBI.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates macrophage infiltration and neuroinflammation after TBI. Its reduction signifies inhibited infiltration and reduced neuroinflammation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: TBI significantly increased MPO-positive neutrophils (p < 0.001) compared to sham. Cl-amidine treatment significantly reduced their number (p < 0.01).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: MPO (Myeloperoxidase) is an enzyme found in neutrophils; MPO-positive neutrophils indicate neutrophil infiltration, part of the acute neuroinflammatory response.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) (at 3 days post-TBI); Cl-amidine treatment following TBI.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates neutrophil infiltration and neuroinflammation after TBI. Its reduction signifies inhibited infiltration and reduced neuroinflammation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: TBI significantly increased IL-1β-positive cells (p < 0.001). Cl-amidine treatment significantly reduced the number of IL-1β-positive cells (p < 0.001) and downregulated its mRNA expression (p < 0.01).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A potent pro-inflammatory cytokine that mediates inflammation and serves as a marker for the pro-inflammatory (M1) microglial/macrophage phenotype.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) (at 3 days post-TBI); Cl-amidine treatment following TBI.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates pro-inflammatory response and neuroinflammation. Reduction signifies a decrease in pro-inflammatory microglial/macrophage activation and overall neuroinflammation after TBI.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (with PAD4 overexpression, with STING activation), lower (with Cl-amidine, with STING inhibition)

Significantly upregulated with PAD4 overexpression (p < 0.01). Significantly decreased with STING antagonist C-176 (p < 0.01).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Represents the pro-inflammatory (M1-like) microglia/macrophage phenotype, which releases detrimental pro-inflammatory mediators.

analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a detrimental inflammatory response and a pro-inflammatory state. Reduction suggests a shift away from this state, promoting an anti-inflammatory environment and ameliorating neuroinflammation.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Protein expression / mRNA expression / Double immunofluorescence staining (cell count)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (with Cl-amidine, with STING/IRE1α inhibition), lower (with PAD4 overexpression, with STING activation)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased by Cl-amidine (p < 0.001 for cells, p < 0.05 for mRNA). Markedly reduced by 2'3'-cGAMP (p < 0.001). Downregulated by PAD4 overexpression (p < 0.05). Upregulated by STING antagonist C-176 (p < 0.001) and IRE1α inhibitor Kira6 (p < 0.001).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An enzyme and marker for the anti-inflammatory (M2-like) microglia/macrophage phenotype, which secretes protective anti-inflammatory mediators, facilitates tissue debris clearance, and promotes tissue repair.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) (at 3 days post-TBI); modulated by Cl-amidine treatment, STING activation (2'3'-cGAMP), PAD4 overexpression, STING inhibition (C-176), or IRE1α inhibition (Kira6).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a shift towards an anti-inflammatory/pro-resolving state, promoting tissue repair and recovery. Its reduction indicates impaired resolution of neuroinflammation and an imbalance towards pro-inflammatory responses.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly downregulated the mRNA expression level (p < 0.01) in Cl-amidine treated group compared to TBI + Vehicle group.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A co-stimulatory molecule and marker for the pro-inflammatory (M1) microglial/macrophage phenotype.

analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates pro-inflammatory microglial/macrophage activation. Its downregulation suggests a reduction in this activation.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An inducible nitric oxide synthase enzyme, a marker for the pro-inflammatory (M1) microglial/macrophage phenotype, contributing to oxidative stress and inflammation.

analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates pro-inflammatory microglial/macrophage activation and oxidative damage. Its upregulation suggests increased detrimental responses, while downregulation indicates reduced pro-inflammatory responses and potential neuroprotection.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly downregulated the mRNA expression level (p < 0.05) in Cl-amidine treated group compared to TBI + Vehicle group.

analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates pro-inflammatory microglial/macrophage activation. Its downregulation suggests a reduction in this activation.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A mannose receptor and marker for the anti-inflammatory (M2-like) microglial/macrophage phenotype, involved in tissue repair and resolution of inflammation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) (at 3 days post-TBI); modulated by Cl-amidine treatment, PAD4 overexpression, or STING inhibition.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates anti-inflammatory microglial/macrophage activation, supporting repair. Its upregulation suggests a promotion of protective responses, while downregulation indicates an imbalance towards pro-inflammatory responses.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Brain (ipsilateral cerebral cortex (CTX), hippocampal CA1, hippocampal DG regions)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: TBI induced significant neuronal loss in ipsilateral CTX (p < 0.001), hippocampal CA1 (p < 0.001), and hippocampal DG (p < 0.05). Cl-amidine significantly ameliorated neuronal loss in ipsilateral CTX (p < 0.01) and hippocampal CA1 (p < 0.05); no significant effect in hippocampal CA3 and DG.

analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) (at 3 days post-TBI); Cl-amidine treatment following TBI.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates neuronal viability. Amelioration of neuronal loss suggests neuroprotection and improved neurological outcome.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher (with STING activation), lower (with IRE1α inhibition)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly upregulated in TBI + Cl-amidine + 2'3'-cGAMP group (p < 0.05). Significantly downregulated by IRE1α inhibitor Kira6 (p < 0.05).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly upregulated (p < 0.001) in the TBI + Cl-amidine + 2'3'-cGAMP group compared to the TBI + Cl-amidine group at 3 days after TBI.
